children: Malaysian palm oil futures dropped more than 1% on Thursday, extending losses for a third consecutive session, as weakness in rival soyoil and anticipated bearish demand and supply figures weighed on sentiment.
The benchmark palm oil contract (FCPOc3) for November delivery on the Bursa Malaysia Derivatives Exchange slid 66 ringgit, or 1.33%, to 4,900 ringgit ($1,207.19) a metric ton at the midday break.

The market traded lower mainly due to weaker soybean oil prices and expectations of an overall bearish Malaysian Palm Oil Board report, said David Ng, a proprietary trader at Kuala Lumpur-based trading firm Iceberg X Sdn Bhd.
The Malaysian Palm Oil Board is expected to release its August demand and supply data later in the day.
Cargo surveyors are also due to release their palm oil export estimates for the September 1-10 period later in the day.

Oil prices held firm after Brent crude breached $100 a barrel, with traders bracing for deeper supply disruptions as Iran and the United States launched their largest attacks on shipping since their six-month-old conflict began. O/R
Stronger crude oil futures make palm a more attractive option for biodiesel feedstock.
Dalian's most-active soyoil contract (DBYcv1) fell 0.95%, while its palm oil contract
shed 1.43%. Soyoil prices on the Chicago Board of Trade (BOcv1) were down 0.5%.
Palm oil tracks the price movements of rival edible oils, as it competes for a share of the global vegetable oils market.
, palm's currency of trade, strengthened 0.22% against the dollar, making the commodity slightly more expensive for buyers holding foreign currencies.

Indonesia is aiming to exert greater influence over the prices of its top commodities in the early stage of operations at its planned new commodity exchange, the country's newly appointed chief regulator said, as Jakarta eyes becoming a global price maker.
Palm oil may retest support at 4,903 ringgit per metric ton, a break below may trigger a fall into the 4,843-4,876 ringgit range, Reuters technical analyst Wang Tao said. TECH/C
